predict.test: Perm (Fin 3) is not commutative: σ * τ ≠ τ * σ
predict.statement: A permutation of order 3 and one of order 2 in `Perm (Fin 3)` never commute.

checks.message: Keep the names and types: `lagrange` and `cauchy` are statements, `ord4 : ℕ`, `σ τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin 3)`.

hints.hint: `statement lagrange {G : Type*} [Group G] (H : Subgroup G) : Nat.card H ∣ Nat.card G` (the bar is `\mid`).

steps: The binders, in order: `{G : Type*}`, `[Group G]`, `[Fintype G]`, `(p : ℕ)`, then the hypotheses `(hp : p.Prime)` and `(hdvd : p ∣ Fintype.card G)`.
The conclusion says some element exists: `∃ x : G, orderOf x = p`.
hints.hint: `statement cauchy {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hdvd : p ∣ Fintype.card G) : ∃ x : G, orderOf x = p`.

steps: List 4, 8, 12, … modulo 12. When do you first reach 0?
An order-3 permutation moves all three points in a cycle 0 → 1 → 2 → 0.
hints.hint: A product of two different swaps: `Equiv.swap 0 1 * Equiv.swap 1 2`.
This always holds when σ has order 3 and τ order 2. Check σ and τ first.
